text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: It costs y to take test x.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provides(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
GRE ::: The GRE test.
FinancialAid ::: Financial aid.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship ::: Economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Tom ::: Tom.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to take test y.
DadOutOfWork(x) ::: x's dad has been out of work.
Premises:
Cost(GRE, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: which is cheaper than $300.
Provides(ETS, FinancialAid, x) → Prove(x, EconomicHardship) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
(SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x)) → Prove(x, EconomicHardship) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
DadOutOfWork(Tom) ∧ FewResources(Tom) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Applying(Tom, GRE) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Provides(ETS, FinancialAid, Tom) ::: ETS provides financial aid to Tom.
